- **`Telephones.java`** — the canonical E.164 converter (the heart of what you asked about). Lines 13-14 define the default country code `"61"` (Australia) applied when there is no `+` prefix. `toE164` (lines 27-44): strips spaces/dashes/brackets; if the number starts with `+` keeps the country code, otherwise assumes `+61` and drops a single leading `0`; validates the result against regex `[0-9]{8,15}` and returns `+` + digits, else `Optional.empty()`.

  ```java
  13  /** Country code assumed when the input carries no explicit '+' prefix (Australia). */
  14  private static final String DEFAULT_COUNTRY_CODE = "61";
  40  if (!digits.matches("[0-9]{8,15}")) { return Optional.empty(); }
  43  return Optional.of("+" + digits);
  ```
